title: OAuth Consent Event With Mixed Signals During Vendor Pilot
description: A user granted consent to a new analytics application during an approved vendor pilot. The app is listed in the pilot documentation, but it requests offline access and mailbox-read permissions broader than the pilot’s stated reporting purpose.
raw_logs: 2026-07-08T17:12:40Z identity_provider event=oauth_consent_granted user=pilot.user@company.example app_name=Insight Analytics Pilot publisher=Insight Analytics Ltd scopes="User.Read Mail.Read offline_access Files.Read" result=success
2026-07-08T17:13:18Z governance_system project=VENDOR-PILOT-77 app_name=Insight Analytics Pilot approved_scope="User.Read Files.Read" status=approved
2026-07-08T17:14:09Z cloud_audit app_name=Insight Analytics Pilot operation=MailItemsAccessed user=pilot.user@company.example count=18
alert_source: Identity Provider, Governance System, Cloud Audit Logs
remediation: Pause or restrict the app pending review, verify vendor permission requirements, revoke excessive scopes if not justified, assess accessed mailbox data, and require updated approval before continued pilot use.
analyst_notes: The vendor pilot is legitimate, but the actual consent scope exceeds the documented scope and the app already accessed mailbox data. The correct response is controlled validation and least-privilege remediation, not immediate closure.
expected_answer: This is an uncertain but high-risk OAuth application event. The model should map it to T1671, assign high severity because of excessive permissions and mailbox access, explain the approved-pilot context, and recommend scope validation and possible consent revocation.
